title: Five-term Hom exactness and outer counit comparison predicates
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, with integer shift functors on $\mathcal C$ (using the shift notation of [def-weil-triangulated-category]); no triangulation or distinguished-triangle hypothesis is imposed. For the two exactness predicates below assume $\mathcal C$ preadditive [def-weil-preadditive-category], and for the image-row predicate assume $\mathcal D$ preadditive as well. Fix objects $A,B,M,G\in\mathcal C$, arrows $s:A\to B$, $t:B\to M$, $\delta:M\to A[1]$, a functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and $K\in\mathcal D$. Define $\operatorname{HomFiveExact}(s,t,\delta,G)$ to mean exactness at the three interior terms of the row
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B[1],G)\xrightarrow{(-s[1])^*}\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],G)\xrightarrow{\delta^*}\operatorname{Hom}(M,G)\xrightarrow{t^*}\operatorname{Hom}(B,G)\xrightarrow{s^*}\operatorname{Hom}(A,G).$$
Each arrow is precomposition by the displayed arrow, and exactness means that the range of the preceding homomorphism equals the kernel of the following one. Define $\operatorname{ImageHomFiveExact}(F,s,t,\delta,K)$ to mean exactness at the three interior terms of
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F(B[1]),K)\xrightarrow{F(-s[1])^*}\operatorname{Hom}(F(A[1]),K)\xrightarrow{F(\delta)^*}\operatorname{Hom}(FM,K)\xrightarrow{F(t)^*}\operatorname{Hom}(FB,K)\xrightarrow{F(s)^*}\operatorname{Hom}(FA,K).$$
No additive or shift-commuting structure on $F$ is assumed in defining this predicate. Finally, for $\epsilon:FG\to K$, define $\operatorname{OuterBijective}(F,A,B,\epsilon)$ to mean that the four functions
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(FT,K),\qquad a\longmapsto\epsilon\circ F(a),\qquad T=B,A,A[1],B[1],$$
are bijective. This last predicate requires only the categories and shifts, without preadditivity. These are definitions of propositions, with no assertion of exactness or bijectivity.
